NgraceChangeDesignContext.Rationale:
The permanent historical baseline control is replaced by one-time discrimination. The retained `spec new` race test and the implicit-supersede test drive the real CLI (the real `ngrace spec new` and `ngrace supersede` verbs) against a disposable project; the two exported-route tests spawn Bun runners that import `mintResolvedBundle` and `mintBundle` directly. In every case the spawned process runs under an isolated-process preload that patches `node:fs.mkdirSync`, plants a competitor `spec.xml` and an unrelated file at the creation boundary **inside that process**, and reports that it fired on stderr (`PROBE: candidate created by another actor after existence checks, before mkdir`). The repaired engine acquires the candidate leaf with a non-recursive `mkdir` whose `EEXIST` refuses, so the competitor survives byte-for-byte. The validation job no longer reads a historical Git object: after the three retirements below, a depth-1 `validate` checkout carries every object the job needs (`HEAD` only).
The old-code checkout existed only to prove that refusal is not vacuous. The replacement is the same proof done once, on a disposable non-Git copy, and recorded here instead of shipped as a permanent suite member. Measured 2026-09-28 UTC on a copy of the repository at base `80cc36f789dc35ef789cfe6d753a39e7115dce76` with `node_modules` symlinked and no `.git`:
- baseline, restored file: `bun test --timeout=0 src/grace-generate.test.ts -t "AC-MINT-EXCLUSIVE: the repaired tree refuses"` exits 0, 1 pass. - mutation A (only the recursive `mkdir`: `mkdirSync(bundlePath, { recursive: true })`): the same command still exits 0, because the shipped `flag: "wx"` exclusive `spec.xml` write still refuses the existing competitor. Half the defect is masked; the red control must drive both halves. - mutation B (recursive `mkdir` together with the non-exclusive `writeFileSync(candidate.specPath, candidate.expectedSpecBytes)`, i.e. the pre-repair F314 pair): the same command exits 1 at `expect(result.exit, "the repaired leaf mkdir refuses").not.toBe(0)`, `Expected: not 0`. - restore: `cp` of the saved `src/grace-generate.ts` is byte-identical to the canonical file, and the same command exits 0 again.
Three retirements remove the job's full-history dependency together. (1) The historical mint worktree test (`git worktree add --detach … 6dd1d95`) hard-fails without the object. (2) The `validateJobCheckoutDepth` assertion hard-fails if `.github/workflows/validate.yml` drops `fetch-depth: 0` while the assertion remains; it asserts the key directly. (3) The declaration-count coverage guard (`coverageRegressions`, `scripts/audit-regressions.test.ts:346`) reads `git show 2434fd4…:<path>` for every existing `*.test.ts` and **fails open** — it `continue`s when `git show` exits non-zero (`:352`), so a depth-1 checkout reports a false green. Applied `AC-COVERAGE-INTACT` (`C-TEST-TIME-BUDGET-4-F173437E`) counted textual `it(`/`test(` declarations, not executed code; it never saw a removed test body that kept its declaration, a newly dead branch, or a file absent at the base. Retiring it leaves no broad suite-wide coverage floor; the targeted mint test does not replace one, and measured executed-code coverage is a later separate bundle.
The mutation is not added to the suite and `src/grace-generate.test.ts` gains no planted-defect test. The permanent suite therefore carries the green direction and none of the mutation, which is the boundary the brief draws.

Alternatives.Alternative: Keep the permanent `6dd1d95` checkout and its `fetch-depth: 0` plus guard. Rejected: it is one of three consumers that force full history on every `validate` checkout, and the discrimination it provides is reproducible once on a disposable copy without shipping an ancestor tree into the normal suite.

Keep the declaration-count coverage guard and merely fetch its base. Rejected: fetching `2434fd4…` to keep a textual declaration count green restores the full-history checkout this bundle removes, and the count still does not measure executed code. The weak guard goes; a real coverage floor is a later separate bundle.

Add a broad executed-code coverage floor in this bundle. Rejected for this slice: it is a new mechanism with its own instrumentation, thresholds, and write scope, and the user wants it measured as a later, separate small bundle with its rationale recorded in project-specific memory outside this repository. Retiring the weak guard here is the honest interim state.

Keep a permanent static test that greps the test file for `6dd1d95` and `worktree` to guard the removal. Rejected: it adds a new test to a bundle whose whole point is to remove regression controls, it changes the metric population for no behavioral reason, and it guards the absence of a mechanism rather than a live behavior. The removals are verified by the plan's file-wide `MustNotContain` assertions and by the execution-time full CI.

Remove `fetch-depth: 0` but keep the `validateJobCheckoutDepth` guard by rewriting it to accept a missing key. Rejected: the guard would then assert the opposite of its original contract and would survive as a contradictory teaching; the guard and its subject go together.

Leave `test-metrics.json` untouched because `artifactIsStale` will not red on a test removal. Rejected: the artifact would silently name three tests that no longer exist. Regeneration is driven from a removed stale artifact, and the relation is pinned, not a duration.

DeferredDecisions.Decision: Measured executed-code coverage is deferred to a later, separate small bundle, with its rationale recorded in project-specific memory outside this repository. This bundle retires the weak declaration-count guard and adds no coverage tooling. The two criteria that name the interim state (`AC-COVERAGE-GUARD-RETIRED`, and `Problem` item 6) state that no broad suite-wide coverage floor remains and that the targeted mint test does not replace one.

The concurrent-worker `ChangeDetector` design is not part of this artifact. Its future interface identifies changes between each dedicated worker workspace and its baseline, and Git is its first replaceable implementation. This mint-test bundle neither implements that adapter nor decides merging. That design gets its own concurrency artifact and will present its own reviewed sequence and class diagrams before its brief. Nothing here forecloses it.

The canonical-spec/plan/execute phrase "the full CI-equivalent verification is close-time only" is read as terminology for the terminal `--assertions final --run-commands` gate, not as a rule that places final validation after apply or archive. The numbered execute sequence already runs that gate before apply confirmation and before `gate apply` / `gate archive`. This bundle does not edit any skill, mirror, CLI, or teaching-surface test; a product-teaching correction, if the maintainer wants the phase names aligned with the ruling that final validation is execution, apply follows, and archive is close, belongs to a separate bundle with its own forced set (`skills/ngrace/ngrace-spec/SKILL.md`, `skills/ngrace/ngrace-execute/SKILL.md`, the two `plugins/ngrace/skills/ngrace/*` mirrors, `scripts/check-teaching-surface.ts`, `scripts/check-teaching-surface.test.ts`, and `test-metrics.json`).

Scenarios.Scenario: A clean checkout at the base with no ancestor object: the normal mint regression suite runs the retained `spec new` race test, the implicit-supersede CLI test, and the two exported-route runner tests, refuses the interspersed competitor, preserves the competitor bytes, and spawns no `git worktree`; the full suite has no historical-control step and the declaration-count coverage guard is gone.

A `pull_request` checkout at the default depth: the `validate` job's checkout carries no `fetch-depth` key; `validate:ci` passes; `validate-marketplace`'s `origin/main...HEAD` diff may return null and fall back to scope-`all`, which is stricter and stays green (the pre-commit hook demonstrates `Scope: all` and PASS); the prepin and recorded-range checks accept a named object-absence, and the scope guard is dormant.

A disposable non-Git copy with the pre-repair defect planted: the retained race test reddens; the copy is restored byte-identical; the retained race test greens. The mutation is never committed to the suite.

The coverage guard driven both ways on a disposable copy: with its base object absent — the depth-1 analogue — a file with every declaration zeroed leaves `coverageRegressions` green (the false green); with the base present the same file reddens; a byte restore greens. The guard is then removed from the file.

A post-close applied-archive tree: the three removed tests are gone, the depth assertion and the coverage guard are gone, `test-metrics.json` names none of the three removed tests, lint is 0/0, the narrow suites pass, and the production and automation paths are byte-unchanged against the base.
